title: Set PCB support pins under a pick-and-place board, clear of underside parts
instruction: Set up the board supports for the next job: stand one support pin upright in each quarter of the white board outline (the thin white lines split it into quarters), the whole pin at least 5 mm inside the outline and at least 3 mm clear of every red area, where the board has parts on its underside that a pin would damage. Keep every pin at least 5 mm from the blue conveyor rails. Take the pins from the black trays, let go of them and move both grippers away from the pins.
context: Surface-mount (SMT) electronics assembly: at every product changeover the line operator sets support pins on the pick-and-place machine's (or stencil printer's) support plate, under where the board stops between the conveyor rails. Spread one to each region of the board, they stop it flexing under the placement head or the squeegee, but they may stand only where the board's underside has no components: a pin under an underside part cracks or dislodges it when the board is clamped, and a pin at a rail fouls the edge clamp. Operators read the clear spots from the board or its setup sheet and find them anew for each product; here they are drawn on the plate, in a different place in each quarter. Unlike fixture tasks that seat a part on its supports, no board is loaded here and nothing is read off a part: the keep-outs are drawn on the plate, and the test is covering all four quarters with one upright pin each in its small clear patch.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Six kinds of thing are on the table, all fixed except the pins. (1) Support plate: a grey steel plate 124 x 220 x 5 mm (124 mm along x), centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0, standing in for a pick-and-place machine's board support plate. (2) Conveyor rails: two blue aluminium bars 6 mm wide, 240 mm long (along y) and 20 mm tall, standing on the table 1 mm outside the plate's two long edges, at x 23.1-23.7 cm and x 36.3-36.9 cm, y -12.0 to +12.0 cm. (3) White lines, white PVC strips 3 mm wide and 1 mm thick fixed on the plate: the board outline, centred on the edges of a 120 x 160 mm rectangle at x 24.0-36.0 cm, y -8.0 to +8.0 cm (the board's edge is the middle of the line), and two quarter lines along x 30.0 cm and y 0 splitting it into four quarters: near left (x 24.0-30.0, y 0 to +8.0 cm), far left (x 30.0-36.0, y 0 to +8.0), near right (x 24.0-30.0, y -8.0 to 0) and far right (x 30.0-36.0, y -8.0 to 0). (4) Red areas, where the board has parts on its underside: eleven red rectangles of red PVC sheet 1 mm thick fixed on the plate (cm): far left x 30.35-35.65, y 3.90-7.65 and x 33.70-35.65, y 0.35-3.50; near left x 24.35-29.65, y 0.35-3.60 and x 28.40-29.65, y 4.00-7.65; near right x 24.35-29.65, y -1.90 to -0.35, x 24.35-29.65, y -7.65 to -6.10, x 24.35-25.00, y -5.70 to -2.30 and x 29.00-29.65, y -5.70 to -2.30; far right x 30.35-35.65, y -3.60 to -0.35, x 30.35-31.00, y -7.65 to -4.00 and x 35.00-35.65, y -7.65 to -4.00. They leave one clear spot in each quarter, in a different place in each, where a pin fits with the margins (its centre within a rectangle 14 to 16.5 mm on a side round x 26.3, y +5.7; x 31.7, y +1.8; x 27.0, y -4.0; and x 33.0, y -5.7 cm); nowhere else on the board is there room for a pin with those margins. (5) Pin trays: two black plastic plates 140 x 40 x 3 mm (140 mm along x), centred at x 19.0 cm, y +23.0 cm and y -23.0 cm. (6) Support pins: six loose steel cylinders 20 mm across and 45 mm tall, 110 g each (solid posts standing in for magnetic-base support pins), standing upright in the trays at x 23.0, 19.0 and 15.0 cm, three at y +23.0 cm and three at y -23.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored on the end state. A pin's 'footprint' is its shadow seen from above (standing upright, a 20 mm circle). It is 'upright' when its axis is within 10 degrees of vertical (either end may be down) and 'on the plate' when its lowest point is within 3 mm of the plate's top. It is 'touching red' when its footprint overlaps or touches a red area while its lowest point is within 5 mm of the plate's top (standing, lying or leaning over the red area), and 'at a rail' when its footprint comes within 5 mm of a rail's while its lowest point is at most 5 mm above the rail's top (on, against or beside a rail). It is 'let go' when neither gripper's finger zone reaches it: every point within a radius of the 38 mm segment running back up the gripper from the point between its finger tips, the radius reaching a finger's outer corner (half the finger gap plus 8 mm, and 13.5 mm across; 57 mm fully open, 31 mm with the fingers 40 mm apart); the zone is round at the finger tips too, so an open gripper hovering less than that over a pin still holds it. A pin 'supports' the quarter holding its centre when it is upright, on the plate and let go, with its whole footprint at least 5 mm inside the board's edge (the middle of the white outline line) and at least 3 mm from every red area; a pin over a quarter line counts for the quarter holding its centre. Score 0 if any pin, spares included, is touching red or at a rail. Otherwise 0.25 for each quarter with at least one supporting pin. A second pin in a quarter adds nothing; spare pins may stay in the trays or anywhere else that breaks neither zero rule; a pin lying down, standing on another pin or on the table, outside the outline, short of a margin or still held supports nothing. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 (no quarter, or one, two, three or all four supported). The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s with a supporting pin in each quarter still (it moved 2 mm or less over the last 0.5 s and is slower than 5 cm/s); otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, a top photo with a millimetre scale laid on the plate shows each pin's footprint against the white lines, red areas and rails, and a square held against each pin shows its tilt.
fidelity: The board is not present (it arrives on the conveyor after the pins are set): its outline and underside parts are drawn on the plate as white lines and red areas, as a setup sheet shows them. The pins are plain steel posts standing by their weight (no magnetic base). The rails are low (20 mm), with no belts or edge clamps; in a machine the board rides on them level with the pins' tops. Rigid bodies, default friction. Gripper heading is not read, so each finger zone is round.
reset_notes: Stand the six pins back upright in the trays at x 23.0, 19.0 and 15.0 cm, three at y +23.0 cm and three at y -23.0 cm. Nothing is consumed; the plate, rails, lines, red areas and trays are fixed.
